title: What Even Is Trading?
hook: Trading isn't predicting the future. You're participating in price movement.

launchpad.outcome: Explain what a trade actually is — market, direction, risk, outcome — before any strategy talk.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Is "I think price is going up" a complete trading plan?

stages.caption: Outcome: price moves, position gains or loses value.

beats.heading: Buy, sell, or short
beats.body: Trading is participating in a financial market by taking a position based on the expectation that price will move. Buy and price rises, or sell/short and price falls — either way there's potential profit. But if price moves against the position, there can be a loss.

beats.heading: Long vs. short
beats.body: Going long means you're positioned to benefit if price rises. Going short means you're positioned to benefit if price falls. Futures let you do either from the start — you don't have to "buy first" like traditional investing.

beats.heading: Trading vs. investing
beats.body: Investing generally focuses on owning an asset and participating in its longer-term growth. Trading generally focuses on profiting from price movement over a defined period. Neither is inherently better — they're different activities.

beats.heading: Trading isn't prediction
beats.body: Our job isn't to know exactly what the market will do next. Our job is to interpret the information price gives us and make rule-based decisions.

blocks.quote: You don't need to know what happens next with certainty to trade. Later, you'll learn to build a thesis, wait for confirmation, and define exactly what would make that thesis invalid.

seeIt.heading: Watch a trade build itself
seeIt.prompt: Every trade is made of the same four pieces. Watch them build on one chart, live.

stages.caption: Market: what are you trading? Every trade starts with a specific market — MNQ, MES, whatever it is.
Direction: do you expect price to rise or fall? This is going long or going short.
Risk: where are you wrong, and how much are you willing to lose? Defined before the trade, not decided emotionally after.
Outcome: price moves. Your position gains or loses value — based on the first three pieces, not on hope.

rounds.question: A trader believes MNQ is likely to decline and takes a position designed to profit from falling prices. What kind of position did she take?

options.label: Short
options.why: A position designed to profit from falling prices is a short — you're positioned to benefit when price falls.

options.label: Long
options.feedback: Long benefits from price rising — the opposite of what's described here.

options.label: Investment
options.feedback: This describes a directional position, not a longer-term investment.

options.label: Limit
options.feedback: A limit is an order type, not a position direction.

rounds.question: A trader's analysis supports higher prices, but price moves against the position. Which statement best represents the AGHF mindset?

options.label: A thesis can be reasonable and still be wrong; risk defines what happens next
options.why: Being reasonable and being right aren't the same thing — that's exactly why risk is defined before the trade, not decided emotionally after.

options.label: The analysis must eventually become correct
options.feedback: Waiting for the market to "prove you right" isn't a risk plan.

options.label: Add another position to improve the entry
options.feedback: Adding to a losing position to average down isn't defined risk — it's hope with more size.

options.label: Wait until price returns to entry
options.feedback: Hoping price comes back isn't a plan — it's refusing to respect your risk.

sayItBack.prompt: Think about it: Why is "I think price is going up" not a complete trading plan? What's missing from that statement?
sayItBack.modelAnswer: "I think price is going up" only covers direction — it doesn't say what market, how much risk I'm willing to take, where I'd be proven wrong, or what the actual outcome plan is. A real trade needs all four pieces: market, direction, risk, and outcome. Direction alone isn't a plan, it's just an opinion.

checklist: Trading is participating in price movement, not predicting the future.
Going long profits from price rising; going short profits from price falling.
Every trade has four pieces: market, direction, risk, and outcome.
Trading isn't about being certain — it's about making structured decisions under uncertainty.

takeaways: Trading is participating in price movement, not predicting the future.
Going long profits from price rising; going short profits from price falling.
Every trade has four pieces: market, direction, risk, and outcome.
remember: Trading isn't about being certain. It's about making structured decisions under uncertainty.
